findings.title: Fix the invalid Ruby closing the header conditional
findings.body: `<%- end if %>` produces invalid Ruby: the trailing `if` has no condition. Every request that finds an existing embedded topic will fail when Rails compiles this template instead of displaying the discussion. Use `<%- end %>` and add a controller test with view rendering enabled; the current mocked controller tests do not exercise template compilation.

findings.title: Sanitize imported HTML before storing it as cooked content
findings.body: Feed content reaches this method directly from PollFeed and is saved with the new `raw_html` cook method, which returns the input without sanitization. `absolutize_urls` only parses and rewrites links; it does not remove scripts, event handlers, or unsafe URL schemes. Consequently, active HTML in a feed (including escaped markup decoded by PollFeed) becomes stored XSS executed on the forum origin when the post is rendered. Sanitize the final imported HTML, including the interpolated source link, before bypassing the normal cooking pipeline.

findings.title: Support feed entries without a content element
findings.body: The poller unconditionally calls `scrub` on `i.content`, but ordinary RSS entries can provide their body only in `description` (or `content:encoded`), and Atom entries can contain only a summary. For these valid feeds, `i.content` is nil and polling raises rather than importing the entry; all subsequent entries are also skipped. Select the available body field and handle missing bodies explicitly, with tests that parse actual RSS and Atom fixtures.

findings.title: Resolve relative references using the article URL
findings.body: The URL conversion treats all leading-slash references as local paths, so `//cdn.example.com/image.jpg` becomes `http://article-host/cdn.example.com/image.jpg`. It also leaves path-relative references such as `images/photo.jpg` and `../other-article` unchanged, causing them to resolve against the forum rather than the imported article. The same problem affects the image loop below. Use URI resolution against the full source URL so imported links and images retain their intended destinations.
